item.title: US withdraws from FIFA Under-17 World Cup in Qatar over safety concerns
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The United States has withdrawn its men’s Under-17 team from the FIFA World Cup in Qatar over safety concerns after a State Department advisory warned Americans to reconsider travel because of the risk of armed conflict. In a letter to players seen by Reuters, US Soccer said it had cancelled the team’s pre-tournament camp and participation “in light of current circumstances”. The federation cited the State Department’s Level 3 travel advisory for Qatar, updated last month, as well as related directives for embassy staff and their families. The advisory referred to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes on civilian airports and critical infrastructure, and warned that hostilities could escalate. US Soccer said it would notify players’ clubs and asked players not to comment publicly until FIFA announced the withdrawal. The 48-team tournament is scheduled to run from November 19 to December 13. The United States had been due to open against Montenegro on November 21, before facing Chile and Algeria in Group J. FIFA told Reuters it had been informed of the decision and would follow the tournament regulations. The governing body said its security assessments remained unchanged and that no new developments had affected the security situation around the tournament. FIFA added that it remained in contact with relevant authorities and looked forward to the tournament, noting that Qatar had hosted several international events in recent months. The United States reached the round of 32 at last year’s edition, also held in Qatar. The country is set to host the tournament annually through 2029. item.title: Customs intercepts 15,375 litres of petrol in Kwara, warns smugglers
item.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), through its Operation Whirlwind, has intercepted 15,375 litres of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), valued at N15.37 million, at various border communities along the Niger-Kwara axis. The National Coordinator of Operation Whirlwind, Mahmood Bello Ishidi, disclosed this on Wednesday during a public auction of the seized petroleum products at the Kwara Area Command headquarters of the NCS in Ilorin. He warned petroleum smugglers that the Service would intensify enforcement operations to curb the illegal movement and diversion of petroleum products across the country’s borders. The seizure, involving 615 jerrycans of 25 litres each, was recorded during intelligence-led operations targeting smuggling networks and illegal diversion of petroleum products across strategic border locations in Kwara State. Ishidi, who spoke on behalf of the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, identified Kaiama, Shiya, Kenu, Boriya, Luma, Baruten, Ilesha-Baruba, Taberu and Salla-Gwanara as some of the locations where the products were intercepted. He said the seizures, with a combined Duty Paid Value of N15,375,000, demonstrated the commitment of the Customs Service to protecting Nigeria’s economic interests and preventing the illegal movement of petroleum products across the country’s borders. Describing petroleum smuggling as economic sabotage, Ishidi warned that the illegal trade undermined government revenue, disrupted domestic supply chains and contributed to artificial scarcity and increased prices of petroleum products. “Beyond depriving the nation of critical revenue, it distorts the supply chain, leading to scarcity and inflated costs that unfairly burden honest Nigerians,” he said. He further warned that petroleum smuggling strengthened organised criminal networks, weakened border security and posed wider threats to national security. The National Coordinator pledged to strengthen intelligence gathering, inter-agency collaboration, operational supervision and enforcement strategies to consolidate the achievements of Operation Whirlwind. “As the newly appointed National Coordinator of Operation Whirlwind, I reaffirm my unwavering commitment to providing purposeful and strategic leadership, enhancing operational effectiveness, and consolidating on the gains and achievements already recorded by the operation,” he stated. Ishidi commended the Comptroller-General of Customs and the management of the Service for their support, while acknowledging the contributions of the Office of the National Security Adviser and the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority to the fight against petroleum smuggling. item.title: ‘Your Sacrifice For A New Nigeria Won’t Be In Vain,’ Obi Assures Nigerians, Condemns Lagos Attack
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has assured Nigerians that their sacrifices and efforts towards building a country they deserve will not be in vain. Obi gave the assurance on Thursday during the party’s town hall meeting in Ikeja, Lagos State. Condemning the attack by suspected thugs before the commencement of the event, the former Anambra State governor said the party would campaign across all parts of Lagos. He also commended party members and supporters for their conduct despite the incident. Obi said Lagos could be better under an NDC government and urged residents to support the party’s governorship candidate, Funso Doherty. Speaking on his plans for the country, the presidential candidate said Nigerians deserved a united nation, adding that he and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, were committed to securing the country. “I and Rabiu Kwankwaso are committed to securing Nigeria,” Obi said. He promised that an Obi-Kwankwaso administration would fight corruption and provide 10,000 megawatts of electricity, insisting that achieving the target was not rocket science. He also pledged to ensure that every ward in the country had a functional primary healthcare centre. Restating his commitment to moving Nigeria from a consumption-driven economy to a production-based one, Obi promised to bring 30 per cent of out-of-school children off the streets and provide them with quality education. “Basic education will be compulsory and free,” he added. On security, the NDC candidate promised to reform the Nigeria Police Force to improve service delivery and strengthen the country’s security architecture. “We want a country that will be manned by people who are competent,” he said. “One of the commitments I have is to improve the welfare of the Nigeria Police. We’ll employ more graduates in our policing system so they can do things differently.” Obi also said President Bola Tinubu was tired and needed to leave office. He urged Nigerians to turn out to vote in the 2027 general elections and remain at their polling units until their votes were counted and transmitted. He further insisted that the voter register must be cleaned up ahead of the elections and that every Nigerian’s vote must count. Earlier, the lawmaker representing Anambra Central Senatorial District in the National Assembly, Victor Umeh, assured Nigerians that those holding the country back would be dismantled. Also speaking, activist Aisha Yesufu urged Nigerians to protect their votes and defend themselves in accordance with the Constitution. item.title: 2027: INEC begins deploying non-sensitive materials
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has begun deploying non-sensitive materials to the zones as it prepares for the 2027 general election. Acting Chairman of the commission, Prof. Rhoda Gumus, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja at a benchmarking meeting with a delegation of Kenya’s Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission IEBC. “Right now, all non-sensitive materials are almost ready. In fact, today as we speak here, the non-sensitive materials have been lifted to some zones now,” Gumus said. She said the commission had completed nine of its scheduled activities and was preparing for the next phase. “We are preparing for the election next year and we have activities lined up. So far, we have been able to complete nine activities and we are still preparing for the next level of activities,” she said. Gumus said the commission’s leadership had just concluded a tour of the country’s six zones to assess their level of preparedness. “The purpose was to go round the zones to see how prepared we are, assess what the zones have put in place, their challenges and what to do. We concluded last week and we can see from our tour that we are really going towards the election proper,” she said. On Permanent Voter Cards PVCs, the acting chairman said production had been completed and distribution to the states was well advanced. “As of today, we can say that PVCs have been produced and the first, second batches, most of the states have received them. Their PVC collection is ongoing. All those who are supposed to be the voters are supposed to receive their PVCs, and if they don’t have them, it is also another challenge,” Gumus said. She added that capacity building was under way for staff at the headquarters and in the states, and that the procurement and deployment of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System BVAS devices were also ongoing. On diaspora voting, Gumus said the commission could not proceed for now because the law did not provide for it. “Here, because we go by the law, in our electoral law, it is not included there, so we cannot go on for the diaspora voting for now until we amend the electoral law,” she said. The acting chairman said the commission had arranged for its directors to hold an interactive session with the Kenyan team and present papers on the work of their departments. Leading the delegation, the Kenyan High Commissioner to Nigeria, Isaac Parashina, said the IEBC team was in Nigeria to benchmark ahead of Kenya’s general election in August 2027. He said the team was studying how Nigeria handled its diaspora population and special voting groups, as Kenya sought to widen voting rights for citizens living abroad. “Currently we have about 12 of them who voted in the last general election, but there is intention to expand to around, I think, 26,” Parashina said, referring to the countries where Kenyans abroad vote. item.title: APC-PCC condemns attack on NDC Lagos town hall, demands swift arrests
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has condemned the attack on the town hall meeting of the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC in Lagos, and called on security agencies to arrest and punish those behind it. The council also condemned other violent attacks at political gatherings in Edo, Cross River and Gombe states. In a statement issued on Thursday, the Spokesperson of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Dele Alake, said the attacks were targeted at party supporters and political leaders across party lines. “We have observed the recent spate of violent attacks at political gatherings in parts of the country. The reported attacks in Edo, Cross River, and Gombe, and other violence targeted at party supporters and political leaders across party lines are condemnable,” the statement said. On the Lagos incident, it said: “Our campaign strongly condemns the disruption of today’s scheduled town hall meeting of the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC in Lagos.” The council urged political parties, politicians and their supporters to show restraint as the campaign season advances. “As we proceed with the electioneering campaign, political parties, politicians, and supporters must restrain themselves and avoid acts that could create needless crisis and public disorder. “We call on the security agencies to be more responsive and alert in preventing political violence of any type and ensure instigators and perpetrators are apprehended and punished in accordance with the law. “Political parties and candidates are enjoined to campaign on issues that uplift the lives of Nigerians and not to instigate violence at political events,” it said. item.title: Lagos APC condemns attack on NDC members, denies involvement
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has condemned the reported attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Ikeja, while dismissing allegations linking the ruling party to the incident. Reacting to the reported disruption of an NDC political gathering on Thursday, the APC State Publicity Secretary, Seye Oladejo, described the allegation as baseless and challenged the opposition party to present any credible evidence to security agencies rather than make public insinuations. In a statement, Oladejo said the allegation was an attempt to drag the APC into an incident without credible evidence linking the party to the disruption. “We consider this allegation not only reckless, baseless and irresponsible but also a desperate attempt to drag Lagos APC into an incident for which the accusers have presented no credible evidence linking the ruling party,” he stated. The party noted that the alleged incident in Ikeja coincided with the official flag-off of its 2027 general election campaign in Epe, where its leadership, elected officials and stakeholders were mobilised. According to the spokesman, the APC could not have abandoned a major statewide political engagement to interfere with an opposition event. “For the avoidance of doubt, Lagos APC categorically rejects any insinuation of involvement, direct or indirect, in the alleged disruption of the said political gathering. We have neither sponsored, encouraged nor participated in any act capable of undermining the constitutional rights of any political party or group to assemble, deliberate and canvass for political support,” he said. Oladejo maintained that the APC’s position as the governing party in Lagos did not make it responsible for every breach of public order in the state. He described the accusation as “a lazy political reflex that substitutes propaganda for investigation and blame-shifting for accountability.” The APC spokesman urged the NDC to submit any credible evidence linking individuals or groups to the incident to the appropriate security agencies. “If the NDC has credible evidence linking any individual or group to the incident, the appropriate course is to present such evidence to the relevant security agencies and allow the law to take its course. Serious criminal allegations should not be established through social media insinuations, emotional outbursts or politically convenient narratives,” he said. While reiterating the party’s commitment to peaceful and issue-based campaigns, Oladejo also expressed concern over what he described as incessant threats by opposition political elements to unleash violence. He called on the Lagos State Police Command and the Department of State Services (DSS) to investigate the incident and take steps to prevent any breakdown of law and order. “Political ambition is not a licence for lawlessness. item.title: Insecurity: Atiku tackles Tinubu as 638 are killed, 64,000 flee Nigeria
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has accused President Bola Tinubu of failing in his fundamental duty to protect Nigerians, following reports that 638 people were killed in insecurity-related incidents in October, while nearly 64,000 others fled violence in northern Nigeria to neighbouring Niger. The figures highlight the scale of the security crisis confronting the country, with Atiku demanding urgent action from the Federal Government to halt the killings, protect vulnerable communities and account for its efforts to restore public safety. In a statement by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku described the figures as a devastating indictment of the country’s security situation. “Behind every number is a Nigerian whose life has been lost, a family in mourning or a community forced to abandon its home. Nigerians should not have to flee across our borders to find safety,” he said. The Centre for Democracy and Development’s October tracker recorded 638 deaths in broader insecurity incidents during the month, with the North-East accounting for 409. Across all security incidents, the figure stood at 640, up from 396 in September. The United Nations also reported that nearly 64,000 people had fled violence in northern Nigeria to Niger since the beginning of 2026, while several hundred others crossed into Benin. Calling for stronger security operations and support for displaced families, Atiku urged the Federal Government to work with neighbouring countries and humanitarian agencies to assist those forced to flee. “The Tinubu administration must make the protection of lives and communities its first responsibility. It must strengthen security in affected areas, support displaced families and work with neighbouring countries and humanitarian agencies to assist those who have fled. Nigerians also deserve a clear account of what is being done to stop the killings and restore safety,” he said. He challenged Tinubu to take responsibility for the worsening security situation rather than offer further explanations. “A government that cannot protect its people has failed in its most basic duty. President Tinubu must stop offering excuses and take responsibility for this worsening crisis. Nigerians need safety now, not another promise,” Atiku said. item.title: Swiss Ebola patient repatriated from Nigeria has recovers
item.description: A Swiss woman who contracted the strain of Ebola linked to the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been discharged from hospital in Geneva, health officials said on Thursday. Read Also: Ebola: FG confirms evacuation of Nigeria’s index patient, husband to Switzerland The patient, the wife of a Swiss embassy employee in Abuja, was evacuated from the Nigerian capital with her husband on October 26. Benoit Carpentier, spokesman for the University Hospitals of Geneva (HUG), said she received appropriate “supportive” care, including hydration and management of any potential complications linked to the disease. “The patient has recovered. She was discharged from hospital yesterday (Wednesday),” he told AFP, confirming a report in the Tribune de Geneve. The woman’s husband showed no symptoms and had his quarantine lifted on November 4. Nigeria announced the case on October 20 and said it was the same Bundibugyo strain of Ebola that has caused the latest outbreak in the DRC. No specific treatment or vaccine exists for the strain, which was officially detected in the central African country in May and has since infected more than 11,000 people, of whom more than 5,400 have died. Cases have also been detected in Uganda and Kenya. Vanguard News The post Swiss Ebola patient repatriated from Nigeria has recovers appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Oyo SDP candidate sues INEC over omission from list
item.description: By Adeola Badru The governorship candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Oyo State, Olusegun Agboola, has accused unnamed political interests of orchestrating a plot to frustrate his 2027 governorship ambition following the omission of his name from the list of candidates published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Agboola, who described his exclusion as illegal, inexplicable and politically motivated, alleged that individuals within rival political parties were working to undermine his candidacy by influencing the electoral commission to exclude him from the official list. The SDP flagbearer, who insisted that he had fulfilled all the necessary electoral requirements, disclosed that he had approached the Federal High Court in Abuja to challenge the omission and seek an order compelling INEC to include his name on the list. In a statement on Thursday, Agboola expressed concern over what he described as the selective exclusion of his name, despite his qualification to contest the forthcoming governorship election. He said, “The illegal and unexplainable omission of my name from the latest INEC published list as the SDP governorship candidate for Oyo State is perplexing. “Of all qualified candidates, my name was singled out and omitted from the published list without any reason from INEC.” Alleging that the development was a deliberate attempt to weaken the SDP’s political standing ahead of the election, Agboola claimed that some politicians in other major political parties were uncomfortable with the party’s agenda and its positions on issues affecting the state. “I have been told that some people from other popular parties are behind it. They are not comfortable with all we stand for, so they want to use INEC to diminish our campaign and suppress all our efforts,” he said. He expressed confidence that the court would intervene and compel INEC to rectify what he described as an electoral anomaly, questioning why a candidate who had complied with established procedures should be forced to seek judicial intervention to secure recognition. “We have followed due process and the court will soon mandate INEC to include our names, but why is that necessary?” he queried. The SDP candidate further alleged that his exclusion was part of a broader scheme by unnamed political interests to manipulate the electoral process and influence the outcome of the 2027 governorship election. “Some people want to use every means possible to doctor the outcome. This is sad for our democracy and shows the integrity of the umpire is damaged if this anomaly is not loudly corrected with a very public announcement from the INEC chairman,” he added. Agboola maintained that Oyo State required practical and sustainable solutions to unemployment, insecurity, inadequate infrastructure and other pressing socio-economic challenges. item.title: 2027: INEC will obey court decision on Atiku’s eligibility – Amupitan
item.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof Joash Amupitan, has said the commission will be bound by court’s decision on whether former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar can contest the 2027 presidential election. Amupitan stated this on Thursday while speaking at Chatham House in London, in response to a question on whether Atiku would be eligible to stand in the election if he failed to overturn the court judgment affecting the leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). The INEC chairman said he was constitutionally obligated to obey court orders, particularly decisions of the Supreme Court, regardless of the political implications. “If he eventually fails, well, I’m obligated under Section 285 of the Constitution of Nigeria to obey every court order, especially if it is from the Supreme Court,” he said. Amupitan, however, expressed concern about the volume of pending litigation involving the electoral commission as preparations for the 2027 general election gather pace. He disclosed that INEC had more than 300 cases pending against it, with the election about 66 days away at the time of the earlier dispute he referenced. “Some of those issues we have with court cases, over 300 cases hanging on the neck of INEC, and elections is just about 66 days away,” he said. He explained that the commission had earlier supported an accelerated hearing of the ADC leadership dispute, insisting that pre-election cases should be resolved early enough to allow INEC to plan its logistics. “When it happened in April, the position of the commission was that matter should be resolved within three weeks,” he said. Amupitan added that the commission had proceeded on the basis of a court directive to suspend action and await the outcome of the legal process, but the matter eventually proceeded to appeal. He also called for reforms to prevent pre-election disputes from disrupting election preparations, proposing that such cases should abate at least six months or one year before an election. “I had advocated in several fora that we pre-election matters should abate at least a year before the election, or let’s say six months, so that we can fix our logistics,” he said. The INEC chairman said the commission had already commenced procurement of sensitive election materials, making unresolved legal disputes a major concern. He warned that implementing court decisions could expose the commission to public criticism, even when it was merely complying with the law. “The danger is that whenever there is such decision, and it’s you to now implement, you become the problem. The problem now is transferred unto you,” he said. The Federal High Court had nullified the leadership of the ADC faction led by former Senate President David Mark, a ruling that has raised questions about the validity of Atiku’s emergence as the party’s presidential candidate. item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has condemned the attack on its supporters by suspected political thugs who invaded a rally organised by the party in Oregun, along Kudirat Abiola Way, Ikeja, Lagos, demanding the immediate investigation, arrest and prosecution of those responsible. The party warned that the attack would not intimidate its members or silence Nigerians, insisting that Nigeria was not a conquered territory and that political participation was not a crime. In a statement issued on Thursday and signed by the Spokesperson of the NDC National Campaign Council, Dr Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, the party described the incident as an unacceptable assault on democracy, citizens’ fundamental rights and freedom of political association. It said no political party or group had a monopoly on Nigeria, adding that nobody had the right to deploy violence, intimidation or thuggery to silence opposing voices. The NDC also called for an end to what it described as the dangerous culture of political violence being witnessed in some states. According to the party, those who believe they can intimidate Nigerians into silence must understand that democracy belongs to the people, not political thugs and their sponsors. The Lagos rally was part of a town hall meeting organised by the NDC as part of its ongoing campaign for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and governorship candidate, Funsho Doherty. item.title: Meet only two countries to have won both men’s and women’s FIFA World Cups
item.description: Only two countries have won both the men’s and women’s FIFA World Cups, highlighting their achievements in international football across the men’s and women’s games. Germany and Spain are the only nations to have lifted both senior FIFA World Cup trophies since the women’s competition was introduced in 1991. While several countries have established themselves as dominant forces in either the men’s or women’s game, Germany and Spain have distinguished themselves by winning football’s biggest international prize in both categories. 1. Germany Germany became the first country to win both the men’s and women’s FIFA World Cups, establishing a record of success across the two competitions. The country’s men’s team has won the World Cup four times, in 1954, 1974, 1990 and 2014, making it one of the most successful national teams in the history of the tournament. Its first triumph came in 1954, when West Germany defeated Hungary 3-2 in the final in Switzerland, producing what became known as the ‘Miracle of Bern’. Germany subsequently won the competition in 1974 on home soil, defeating the Netherlands 2-1 in the final, before claiming a third title in 1990 with a 1-0 victory over Argentina in Italy. The country’s fourth triumph came in Brazil in 2014, when Mario Gotze scored the winning goal in extra time to secure a 1-0 victory over Argentina. Germany’s success has also extended to the women’s game, where the national team won consecutive FIFA Women’s World Cup titles in 2003 and 2007. In 2003, Germany defeated Sweden 2-1 after extra time in the final, with Nia Kunzer scoring the golden goal to deliver the country’s first women’s world title. Four years later, the team successfully defended its crown in China, defeating Brazil 2-0 in the final through goals from Birgit Prinz and Simone Laudehr. With four men’s titles and two women’s titles, Germany has won six senior FIFA World Cups combined, the highest total among countries to have won both competitions. 2. Spain Spain became the second country to achieve the double after winning the FIFA Women’s World Cup in 2023, joining Germany in the exclusive group. The country’s men’s team first conquered the world in 2010, when it defeated the Netherlands 1-0 after extra time in the final in South Africa. Andres Iniesta scored the decisive goal in the 116th minute, securing Spain’s maiden World Cup title under coach Vicente del Bosque. The triumph marked the culmination of a remarkable period for Spanish football, following the country’s victory at the 2008 European Championship. Thirteen years later, Spain’s women’s team delivered another historic achievement by winning its first FIFA Women’s World Cup. Spain defeated England 1-0 in the 2023 final in Sydney, Australia, with Olga Carmona scoring the decisive goal in the first half. item.title: Katsina APC Campaign Council Condemns Funtua Violence, Says Perpetrators Will Face Justice
item.description: The Tinubu/Dikko 2027 Campaign Council of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has condemned attacks by suspected political thugs during its campaign tour of the Funtua Senatorial District in Katsina State, assuring residents that those responsible will be brought to justice. The Director-General of the Campaign Council, Arch. Ahmed Musa Dangiwa, gave the assurance on Thursday while briefing journalists at the council’s headquarters in Dandagoro, Katsina. Dangiwa expressed sympathy to victims of the attacks in Malumfashi and Yankara, describing the incidents as unfortunate and contrary to the spirit of democratic engagement. He said the Katsina State Government had directed security agencies to intensify investigations and ensure that those responsible were apprehended and prosecuted. Damaged APC campaign vehicle. The campaign council chief also said measures had been put in place to prevent a recurrence, while condemning political violence, intimidation and destruction of property, regardless of those involved. He commended security agencies for their response but urged them to conduct thorough investigations into all reported cases and ensure that anyone found culpable faced the full weight of the law. Dangiwa also called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to expedite the signing of a broader peace accord, noting that political parties in the state had already signed a peace agreement. He appealed to opposition parties to review their campaign schedules and remove campaign billboards where necessary to prevent avoidable clashes and ensure smooth political activities across the state. The Director-General thanked APC stakeholders, supporters and media practitioners for their cooperation during the 11-day campaign tour of the Funtua Senatorial District, which covered all 11 local government areas. With the completion of the Funtua phase, Dangiwa announced that the campaign council would move to the Daura Senatorial District before proceeding to the Katsina Senatorial District. He said the next phases would build on lessons from the Funtua tour through improved coordination, logistics and media engagement, while sustaining direct interactions with communities and showcasing the development achievements of the Tinubu and Radda administrations. The council also urged APC members and supporters to remain united, disciplined and law-abiding, while respecting the rights of supporters of other political parties. Dangiwa reiterated the council’s commitment to issue-based campaigns, peaceful democratic participation and continued engagement with residents of Katsina State. He acknowledged Governor Dikko Umaru Radda, his deputy, traditional rulers, elected representatives, party executives, campaign coordinators, security agencies, media organisations and residents of the Funtua Senatorial District for their contributions to what he described as a successful first phase of the statewide campaign. item.title: Over N10trn invested in power sector since privatisation – FG
item.description: –Seeks private sector led growth By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Federal Government has called for increased private sector investment in the electricity industry, saying over N10 trillion spent on the sector since privatisation has not been sufficient to address its infrastructure and financing challenges. Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, FGN Power Company Limited, Mr Kenny Anuwe, made the call on Thursday at the sixth annual conference of the Power Correspondents Association of Nigeria (PCAN) in Abuja. Anuwe, who delivered the keynote address at the conference themed, “$1 Trillion Economy: Nigeria’s Roadmap to Reliable and Affordable Power Supply”, said government funding alone could not provide the scale of investment required to support Nigeria’s ambition of becoming a $1 trillion economy. He said: “The government has invested over N10 trillion in the electricity sector since the advent of privatisation. But is it enough? How much money is enough? If the government didn’t invest that money, the industry would not be standing today.” However, he lamented that the government still accounted for more than 95 per cent of new infrastructure investments in the sector, describing the situation as unsustainable. According to him, the industry must move away from overdependence on public funding by creating an investment-friendly environment that would attract private capital. “We need to change our minds about the reality that the government cannot do everything. The government can provide the enablers, infrastructure, delivery and market conditions under which public and private capital can perform effectively,” he said. Anuwe called for simplified institutional and regulatory arrangements, clear responsibilities, predictable regulations, bankable projects and faster decision-making to encourage investors. He disclosed that FGN Power Company was targeting a $2.3 billion investment programme, comprising $1.3 billion from Europe and $1 billion from China. He added that the company was working towards raising at least $1 billion in capital, with the Africa Finance Corporation indicating willingness to match the amount, while additional financiers were expected to mobilise about $18 billion into the electricity sector. The FGN Power boss said the company was also exploring alternative financing arrangements, including viability financing and blended finance, to attract institutional and private investors. On infrastructure development, he said the Presidential Power Initiative had completed its pilot phase and was implementing the first phase of transmission substations and lines, with most of the projects expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027. He said the second batch of Siemens substations, comprising 12 facilities, was expected to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to necessary financing approvals. item.title: Ebonyi pensioners endorse Nwifuru for second term
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP) has endorsed Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, for a second term in office ahead of the 2027 governorship election, citing his administration’s payment of outstanding pension and gratuity arrears dating back to 1996. The union also conferred an award on Nwifuru as the most pensioner-friendly governor in recognition of what it described as his commitment to the welfare of retired workers in the state. The endorsement was announced during the presentation of the award to the governor in Ebonyi State. The National President of NUP, Comrade Godwin Abumisi, represented by his deputy, Abdulahi Onuh, commended Nwifuru for clearing the backlog of pensions and gratuities owed to retired workers from 1996. Onuh described the achievement as significant, saying the governor had distinguished himself through his administration’s intervention in the welfare of pensioners. He said, “Clearing pensions and gratuity of pensioners from 1996 till date is not a small number of years. The Governor has written his name in gold. “While in Kano, I thought that the Governor of Kano State is number one. I never knew that coming to Ebonyi State, the Kano Governor will be number two. “To clear a backlog of pensions and gratuity from 1996 till date is a very big achievement. May God elongate the life of Ebonyi Governor. The Governor has done a lot.” He also commended the state government over plans to extend the state health insurance scheme to retirees, describing the initiative as another important intervention in their welfare. The NUP national leadership, however, urged the state government to implement pension increases and harmonisation of benefits, noting that pension increments were provided for under the Constitution. Onuh called on pensioners to reciprocate the governor’s gesture by voting for him in the 2027 election. He said, “You are indebted to the Governor. Use your PVCs and show him appreciation by voting for him in the 2027 general election. “When you go home, off your clothes and tell your children that as of two years back, they were taking you to the hospital every week. You were calling your children both home and abroad, bring me my medical allowance. “But the Governor has reduced the strength of your children in Nigeria and outside. Go and pay him back. Tell your children, tell your in-laws to pay the Governor back by voting for him.” Also speaking, the Ebonyi State Chairman of NUP, Comrade Anna Ibiam, said retired workers had endured years of unpaid pensions and gratuities before Nwifuru assumed office. She said some pensioners died while waiting for their entitlements, adding that the governor’s administration had changed the situation through regular pension payments and the clearance of outstanding gratuities. “Many of our colleagues died waiting without receiving their gratuity. item.title: Reps threaten action against Science Minister over bill
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has threatened legislative action against the Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr Kingsley Tochukwu Udeh, over his failure to attend a public hearing on a bill seeking to establish a National Research and Innovation Development Fund. The lawmakers warned that the ministry’s absence could delay the proposed legislation and undermine President Bola Tinubu’s efforts to attract international research grants and funding from development partners, donor agencies, United Nations organisations and Nigerians in the diaspora. The House Committee on Science and Technology expressed displeasure that neither the minister nor the ministry’s Permanent Secretary or any senior representative attended the hearing, despite the ministry’s direct responsibility for the subject matter of the bill, HB 2821. The committee also noted that the proposed legislation was sponsored by the executive and transmitted to the National Assembly by President Tinubu. Speaking at the hearing, a member of the committee, Hon. Ahmed Usman Jaha, representing Chibok, Damboa and Gwoza Federal Constituency of Borno State, described the ministry’s absence as a possible act of sabotage against the working relationship between the executive and legislative arms of government. Jaha, who spoke on behalf of the committee, said it was difficult to understand why a ministry directly concerned with an executive-sponsored bill of national importance would fail to participate in its consideration. “Unfortunately, some members of the executive are by extension sabotaging this relationship. The reason why I call it sabotage is that I see no reason whereby the executive can present a bill to the House for consideration, and that bill has national importance, but the ministry responsible for it will not show up,” he said. He disclosed that the committee had invited the Ministers of Justice, Innovation, Science and Technology, Education, Environment, Agriculture and Food Security, Health, Livestock Development, and Industry, Trade and Investment, alongside other stakeholders, to contribute to the legislative process. However, none of the invited ministers attended the hearing. Jaha said the absence of the Science and Technology Minister was particularly concerning, insisting that either the minister or the Permanent Secretary should have appeared before the committee. “We are not averse to the Ministry of Justice and other ministries that are not directly linked to the bill. But our concern this time around is the Ministry of Science and Technology. If any minister may not have time to attend, they may end up sending representatives. But the Minister of Science and Technology himself, who is more or less the sponsor of the bill, or in a worst-case scenario, the Permanent Secretary, must show up,” he said. item.title: ‘We’ll Be Refined And Rugged In 2027,’ Aisha Yesufu Tells NDC Supporters After Lagos Attack
item.description: A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Aisha Yesufu, has warned that the party and its supporters will not tolerate intimidation ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that they will be both “refined and rugged” in their political engagements. Speaking at the NDC town hall meeting in Lagos on Thursday, Yesufu said the party would not allow anyone to intimidate its members, insisting that supporters would stand up against attacks. “In 2023 we were refined, in 2027 we will be refined and rugged. Nobody has monopoly of madness and anybody wey say him dey crase we go send am go psychiatric hospital. We are not slaves, we are citizens. This campaign is not Peter Gregory Obi campaign, it is our campaign,” Yesufu said. ﻿ Her remarks followed an attack on NDC supporters ahead of the town hall meeting at the Classic Event Centre in the Oregun area of Lagos. Suspected thugs reportedly stormed the venue around 11am, attacking supporters and disrupting preparations for the gathering. Some attendees fled for safety as the attackers reportedly wielded cutlasses, cudgels and other objects. The incident left some supporters injured and vehicles damaged, while a journalist covering the event was also reportedly assaulted and had his recording equipment taken. The confrontation later spilled onto Kudirat Abiola Way, disrupting traffic before police operatives arrived and fired tear gas to disperse the crowd. The town hall meeting was organised as part of the NDC’s mobilisation activities ahead of the 2027 elections, with the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, expected to attend. item.title: ‘I’m Here’, Fubara Declares As Wike Inaugurates Rainbow Coalition, APC Campaign Council In Rivers
item.description: The Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, on Thursday, declared his unwavering support for the All Progressives Congress (APC), stating that he is fully involved in the Rainbow Coalition movement. He made the declaration as the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, Nyesom Wike, inaugurated members of the Rivers APC Campaign Council and Rainbow Coalition in the State. He urged members to demonstrate through their actions that they are committed to the political cause ahead of the 2027 general elections. The governor said he expected members to be honest about their political convictions, stressing that those unwilling to support his position should openly take a different path rather than engage in double-dealing. He said his political decision is firm and would not be different whether expressed publicly or privately. “Don’t say you’re openly with me, and behind you’re doing a different thing. I’m here, and I say it boldly anywhere, any day, in private and in secret. I have taken this position, and anybody who says he is not with me, gently go your way.” Gov. Fubara also urged members to put past political differences behind them, noting that the new campaign council has brought together a broader spectrum of political stakeholders, including some who were previously in opposition. He described the expanded composition of the council as an advantage that could strengthen the coalition’s chances if members worked together. Recalling the 2023 general elections, the governor said a similar political structure had helped secure victory for him and President Bola Tinubu, expressing confidence that the new council could deliver even more votes in 2027. He challenged members to approach the assignment with determination, insisting that electoral success would depend on their willingness to work collectively towards a common objective. “If we take it as a serious responsibility, a serious task that must be achieved, we will come out decisive, with a stronger vote that is more than what we did in 2023.” The governor congratulated members of the inaugurated council and assured those who were not included in the initial list that additional committees would be constituted and the structure could still be expanded. He expressed appreciation to the council’s leadership and other political stakeholders for their efforts, praying for success in the task ahead. item.title: US Does Not ‘Need A Deal With Iran’, Says Trump
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Thursday said he was directing Vice President JD Vance to focus solely on domestic anti-fraud efforts and not negotiations with Tehran. “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” Trump wrote on Truth Social. The development was after the US President defended the war against Iran Wednesday at a US Veterans Day commemoration that saw his defense secretary publicly admonished for a lack of decorum. “The bravery and skill of our amazing American warriors has absolutely been incredible,” Trump said in an address at Arlington National Cemetery just outside Washington. “When this conflict is over, and it will be soon, the entire world will be a much safer and better place, more peaceful place, and a place without the kind of danger that we had to suffer.” U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks during a ceremony in honor of Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery on November 11, 2026 in Arlington, Virginia. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP The war, which began on February 28 with US and Israeli strikes against Iran, has so far cost the lives of 23 US service members and wounded several hundred more, according to the latest Pentagon figures. Trump said in his remarks that the conflict was started not by Washington but by Tehran, which “has been waging war on America since 1979.” U.S. President Donald Trump and U.S. Vice President JD Vance participate in a wreath-laying ceremony in honor of Veterans Day at The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery on November 11, 2025 in Arlington, Virginia. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP He stressed that US forces were acting to halt Iran’s capacity to build a nuclear weapon. Trump, 80, attended a wreath-laying ceremony at the cemetery’s Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, a sacred symbol for America’s lost service members. During his speech before troops, veterans and top officials in his administration, Trump namechecked Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who was in attendance, saying he had “done a fantastic job.” Republicans in the US House of Representatives on Tuesday blocked an effort — launched by an outgoing Republican lawmaker — to impeach Hegseth for allegedly waging war without congressional authorisation and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief. item.title: UNIJOS Appoints First Female Vice Chancellor In 50-Year History
item.description: The University of Jos has appointed Professor Patricia Mamko Lar as its 11th substantive Vice Chancellor, making her the first woman to occupy the position since the establishment of the institution. Her appointment was announced on Thursday by the Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the University’s Governing Council, Senator Grace Folashade Bent, during a special meeting of the 15th Governing Council. Professor Lar takes over from Professor Tanko Ishaya, whose tenure as Vice Chancellor has come to an end. Presenting the letter of appointment to the incoming Vice Chancellor, Senator Bent charged her to remain focused in the discharge of her responsibilities as she prepares to lead the university. Her emergence marks a historic milestone for the University of Jos, as she becomes the first female Vice Chancellor in the institution’s history and the 11th substantive head of the university. item.title: Five key allies of Peter Obi who parted ways with him after 2023
item.description: ‎ The recent decision by Yunusa Tanko a leading figure in the Obidient Movement, to accept an appointment as Director-General of the presidential campaign council of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) candidate has once again drawn attention to the growing list of notable political associates who have distanced themselves from former Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi. ‎ ‎Since the conclusion of the 2023 presidential election, Obi has remained one of the country’s most influential opposition politicians. ‎However, several key figures who played important roles in his campaign, political structure, or movement have either left the Labour Party, aligned with other political interests, or openly criticized his political direction. Obi is presently the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate for the 2027 election. ‎ ‎These defections have triggered renewed debate about the cohesion of the political movement that emerged around Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign. 2027: IGP warns officers against compromise Thugs attack Pantami’s campaign rally in Gombe ‎ ‎While Obi continues to command a loyal support base across the country, the departure of several high-profile associates underscores the challenge of maintaining political unity and building a durable structure ahead of the next electoral cycle. ‎ However, his present alliance with Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, the leader of Kwankwasiyya Movement, is seen by many as a plus to him. ‎ ‎Below are five of such most prominent names. ‎ ‎ YUNUSA TANKO tanko yunusa ‎ ‎Perhaps the latest and most symbolic departure is that of Yunusa Tanko, who served as National Coordinator of the Obidient Movement and was one of the most visible defenders of Obi after the 2023 election. ‎ ‎Tanko was a key mobiliser of Obi’s support base across the country and regularly represented the movement on national television and at political events. However, he recently accepted an appointment as Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council of SDP presidential candidate, Adewole Adebayo, effectively moving away from Obi’s political camp. ‎ ‎YUSUF DATTI BABA-AHMED ‎ ‎As Obi’s running mate in the 2023 election, Yusuf Datti Baba-Ahmed was one of the central figures of the Labour Party ticket. ‎Although he has not openly defected to another political camp in the manner of some of Obi’s former associates, reports indicate that he publicly expressed disagreements with aspects of Obi’s political direction, fueling speculation about differences within the former presidential ticket. ‎ ‎KENNETH OKONKWO ‎ ‎Actor, lawyer and politician, Kenneth Okonkwo was one of the most vocal spokespersons of the Obi campaign during the 2023 presidential race. ‎ ‎In July 2024, he announced his exit from the Labour Party and openly criticized Obi’s handling of the party’s leadership crisis.
